subject.title: telegram: track re-enable criteria for richMessages default-on (Bot API 10.1 client rollout)

question: What verified Telegram client coverage is sufficient to permit `channels.telegram.richMessages` to become default-on?
rationale: OpenClaw cannot negotiate rendering capability across the multiple Telegram clients a recipient may use, so the acceptable unsupported-client population is a product-policy choice rather than an implementation fact.

options.title: Require Web and macOS parity
options.body: Keep default-off until Telegram Web A/K and current macOS group and forwarded-message paths pass direct live tests.

options.title: Keep permanent opt-in
options.body: Retain explicit opt-in indefinitely because recipient client capability is not observable bot-side.

options.title: Accept a documented long tail
options.body: Approve default-on after a named mainstream-client matrix passes while explicitly accepting listed unsupported clients.

recommendation.title: Require Web and macOS parity
recommendation.body: Keep default-off until Telegram Web A/K and current macOS group and forwarded-message paths pass direct live tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent ownership signal on the exact default, inheritance, and compatibility surface.
